claim: PKCE protects OAuth public clients against authorization code interception attacks
normalized: pkce protect oauth public client against authorization code interception attack

sources.title: RFC 7636 — Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients

trust.earned_rationale: Normative IETF standard; primary source for PKCE.

sources.quote: PKCE protects public clients using the authorization code flow against authorization code interception attacks via the code_verifier / code_challenge exchange.
sources.stance_note: The RFC's stated purpose: mitigate code interception on public clients.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice (RFC 9700)

trust.earned_rationale: Current IETF best practice; supersedes older guidance where they conflict.

sources.quote: Clients MUST use PKCE with the authorization code grant — for public and confidential clients alike.
sources.stance_note: Extends the requirement beyond public clients to all authorization code flows.

sources.title: Okta Developer Docs — PKCE Flow

trust.earned_rationale: Vendor documentation from a major identity provider; consistent with RFCs.

sources.quote: Okta recommends PKCE for all applications using the authorization code flow where the client cannot be fully trusted.
sources.stance_note: General vendor guidance aligned with the standards.

sources.title: Auth0 Docs — Authorization Code Flow with PKCE

trust.earned_rationale: Vendor documentation; accurate but scoped to Auth0's implementation.
